description: Hand-build the 4P4D PD-disaggregated topology (4-GPU prefill + 4-GPU decode) with SGLang native PD serving the SAME preview DSpark weights, then run the identical bench sweep for a like-for-like comparison. Depends on FEAT-002 completing its bench (both topologies share the one weight copy). Prefer SGLang native PD (--disaggregation-mode prefill|decode + nixl transfer backend + router) to keep the same weights/stack as TP8 for comparability; vLLM PD needs the different NVFP4 repo and is NOT the first choice. First tear down sglang-tp8 (docker rm -f) and confirm all 8 GPUs return to 0 MiB before launching PD.
steps: Tear down TP8: `docker rm -f sglang-tp8`; confirm `nvidia-smi` shows all 8 cards at 0 MiB before proceeding (avoid GPU collision).

Adapt the proven SGLang PD reference scripts/docker-compose-pd-v4flash-b300.yaml for a 4P4D layout on preview DSpark: prefill engine on GPUs 0-3 (TP4) and decode engine on GPUs 4-7 (TP4) -- i.e. ONE prefill + ONE decode engine (4P4D = 4-card prefill + 4-card decode), not the reference's 3x(tp2)+1x(tp2). Pin physical cards explicitly with docker `--gpus '"device=0,1,2,3"'` (prefill) / `'"device=4,5,6,7"'` (decode) -- do NOT use --gpus all (it overrides NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and collided engines in the prior vLLM run).

Carry over proven PD settings from the reference: --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl (mooncake does NOT work for same-node PD); --disaggregation-mode prefill/decode with distinct --disaggregation-bootstrap-port per engine; keep dp-attention OFF (it caused AssertionError + GPU mem drop to 0); set env SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384, SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=1800, SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=1800. Replace stable-weight+megamoe+EAGLE with preview weights + --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4; keep DSpark on the decode side (--speculative-algorithm DSPARK) or as SGLang PD requires. Use base64-encoded scripts/compose to avoid send-command quoting issues.

Launch a sglang_router (launch_router --pd-disaggregation --prefill <url> <bootstrap-port> --decode <url> --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30080) so the PD endpoint is on the SAME loopback 127.0.0.1:30080 as TP8, letting the identical bench command be reused.

Poll each engine's health and the router: `curl -sf` on the prefill port, decode port, and router :30080/health. Confirm via nvidia-smi that memory splits GPUs 0-3 (prefill) vs 4-7 (decode) with no collision. Cold start ~20-25 min. Smoke one /v1/chat/completions through the router to prove prefill -> KV transfer -> decode -> stream end to end.

If preview DSpark + PD does not work on this SGLang version (spec-decode+PD incompatibility, KV layout mismatch, missing/failing transfer backend), capture the full error, judge the root cause, and try reasonable fixes: switch transfer backend (nixl<->mooncake), disable DSpark on the decode side first to validate the base PD path then re-add it, adjust mem-fraction. Record every blocker and its resolution in findings.

Run the IDENTICAL bench sweep (same 口径 as FEAT-002: 40k in / 1.5k out, c=1/2/4/8/16, same NP map, same validated --random-range-ratio) against 127.0.0.1:30080, writing to /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/. Background with nohup + poll. Capture the same metrics; note that DSpark accept stats may not be surfaced through the PD router (as observed in the prior vLLM PD run) -- if so, confirm DSpark active from engine startup logs and document the limitation.
acceptance_criteria: Prefill engine healthy on GPUs 0-3 and decode engine healthy on GPUs 4-7 (nvidia-smi confirms the 0-3 vs 4-7 memory split, no collision).
Router `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:30080/health` returns 200 and a smoke chat completion through the router returns a valid response (PD path proven end to end).
bench_serving completes all 5 levels (c=1,2,4,8,16) with 0 failed requests, producing /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/c{1,2,4,8,16}.jsonl + .log.
The exact PD route used (native SGLang PD, transfer backend, whether DSpark stayed on decode) and any blockers + fixes are recorded in findings.
verification: SSM send-command `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:30080/health` returns 200 while PD engines run.
SSM send-command `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used --format=csv,noheader` shows nonzero memory on all of 0-7 split as prefill(0-3)/decode(4-7).
SSM send-command `ls -la /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/ && grep -h 'Successful requests\|Mean TPOT' /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/c*.log` shows all 5 files with completed requests.
findings:
COMPLETED 2026-09-14. All 4 acceptance criteria met. 4P4D PD stood up cleanly on FIRST try with native SGLang PD + nixl transfer backend + DSpark on decode; full identical bench sweep ran with 0 failed requests. PD engines + router LEFT RUNNING per boundaries; TP8 artifacts in /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out/ untouched.

PD ROUTE USED (exact): SGLang NATIVE PD disaggregation (NOT vLLM). Transfer backend = nixl (mooncake NOT attempted; nixl worked first try as the reference predicted). ONE prefill engine GPUs 0-3 (TP4, --disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 9000, port 30000) + ONE decode engine GPUs 4-7 (TP4, --disaggregation-mode decode --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 9300, port 30300) = true 4P4D. DSpark STAYED ON the decode side (--speculative-algorithm DSPARK) and is fully compatible with the nixl PD path on this build -- no KV-shape mismatch, no fallback needed. sglang_router (launch_router --pd-disaggregation --prefill http://127.0.0.1:30000 9000 --decode http://127.0.0.1:30300 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30080) exposes the PD endpoint on the SAME loopback 127.0.0.1:30080 as TP8, so the identical bench command was reused.

(0) TEARDOWN: `docker rm -f sglang-tp8` -> confirmed all 8 GPUs back to 0 MiB before launching PD (no collision risk). Weights reused in place at /opt/dlami/nvme/models/deepseek-ai__DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark (NOT re-downloaded).

(1) LAUNCH: three base64-encoded scripts written to /opt/dlami/nvme/{launch_pd_prefill.sh,launch_pd_decode.sh,launch_pd_router.sh}. Physical cards pinned EXPLICITLY with docker `--gpus '"device=0,1,2,3"'` (prefill) / `'"device=4,5,6,7"'` (decode) -- did NOT use --gpus all. NO NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES env on the engines (the --gpus device= form is authoritative). Engine flags matched TP8 stack for comparability: --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --trust-remote-code --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 --enable-metrics --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4; PD-specific: --disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl + --disaggregation-mode + distinct --disaggregation-bootstrap-port. Env per engine: SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384, SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=1800, SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=1800. dp-attention left OFF (server_args confirmed enable_dp_attention=False). Router: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" (no GPU), --worker-startup-timeout-secs 60 --request-timeout-secs 3600.

(2) STARTUP (clean, NO errors, NO OOM at mem-fraction 0.90 on TP4): cold start ~11-12 min wall (02:42 launch -> prefill ready 02:51, decode ready 02:54). Both engines: 'Detected fp8 checkpoint', flashinfer_mxfp4 loaded as Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod ('FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE deferred finalize is disabled'), 48/48 shards, DeepSeek V4 MHC prenorm prewarm, DeepGEMM warmup 16384, FlashInfer autotune, cuda-graph capture. Then 'Disaggregation warmup requests completed for all 1 DP ranks' -> 'End of disaggregation warmup' -> 'The server is fired up and ready to roll!' on BOTH engines -- i.e. the PD bootstrap handshake succeeded and a warmup req already flowed prefill->KV-transfer->decode. DSPARK CONFIRMED on decode: all 4 decode TP ranks logged 'Draft checkpoint bundles a DSpark head; loading draft arch DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark.' Decode server_args confirmed disaggregation_mode='decode', disaggregation_transfer_backend='nixl', disaggregation_bootstrap_port=9300, speculative_algorithm='DSPARK', moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_mxfp4', kv_cache_dtype='fp8_e4m3', enable_dp_attention=False. Prefill /health=200, decode /health=200.

(3) ROUTER: launched sglang-pd-router, workers activated healthy. BENIGN WARN observed and left as-is: 'Model ... has conflicting load_balance_method: prefill=Some("follow_bootstrap_room"), decode=Some("round_robin")' -- this is normal for PD (each side uses its own policy: prefill follows the bootstrap room, decode round-robins); router still reports both workers healthy and routes correctly. Router /health=200 on :30080.

(4) SMOKE through router: /v1/chat/completions ('capital of France?') -> 'The capital of France is Paris.' finish_reason=stop. Proves router -> prefill(0-3) -> nixl KV transfer -> decode(4-7, DSpark) -> stream end to end.

(5) GPU SPLIT (no collision): prefill GPUs 0-3 each ~253.0-253.4 GB, decode GPUs 4-7 each ~252.2-252.3 GB. Memory splits cleanly 0-3 (prefill) vs 4-7 (decode) exactly as required; the prior vLLM run's --gpus all collision did NOT recur (explicit device= pinning worked).

(6) RANGE-RATIO / kou-jing VALIDATION (c=1 np=2): --random-range-ratio 1.0 yields FIXED 40k input through the PD router too (#Input tokens=80000 = 40000 each, #Output tokens=3000 = 1500 each). IDENTICAL kou-jing to FEAT-002 TP8 confirmed: backend sglang-oai, --dataset-name random --random-input-len 40000 --random-output-len 1500 --random-range-ratio 1.0, c in {1,2,4,8,16}, NP map {1:8,2:8,4:12,8:24,16:48}.

(7) FLUSH-CACHE RACE: reused the FEAT-002 manual-pre-flush pattern against the ROUTER :30080 (DROPPED --flush-cache from the bench command; sweep_pd.sh POSTs /flush_cache retrying until 200 on the idle router before each level, settles 2s, then runs bench without --flush-cache). Worked perfectly: flush returned 200 on attempt 1 at every level, no race, no aborted run. NOTE: the router DOES proxy POST /flush_cache to the engines (returns 200), so the manual pre-flush is effective through the PD router.

(8) SWEEP RESULT (4P4D, fixed 40k in / 1.5k out, --random-range-ratio 1.0, backend sglang-oai via router 127.0.0.1:30080, bench run inside sglang-pd-decode container). All 5 levels: completed == num_prompts, 0 FAILED. Artifacts in /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/: c{1,2,4,8,16}.jsonl + .log (+ validate_c1.jsonl/.runlog + sweep.runlog).
  c=1  (np8):  reqs 8/8  | TPOT med/p90/p99 = 1.22/1.40/1.47 ms | TTFT med/p90/p99 = 1834/4000/4003 ms | ITL med/p90/p99 = 7.07/7.12/7.20 ms | out tput 362.8 tok/s | total 10036 tok/s
  c=2  (np8):  reqs 8/8  | TPOT 1.26/1.94/2.12 | TTFT 2852/4923/5408 | ITL 7.10/7.72/7.85 | out 523.9 | total 14493
  c=4  (np12): reqs 12/12 | TPOT 1.33/1.65/1.84 | TTFT 3780/5781/6362 | ITL 7.13/8.27/10.96 | out 814.5 | total 22535
  c=8  (np24): reqs 24/24 | TPOT 1.32/1.42/1.52 | TTFT 9614/11653/12395 | ITL 7.12/7.76/8.67 | out 880.3 | total 24355
  c=16 (np48): reqs 48/48 | TPOT 1.32/1.45/1.56 | TTFT 21929/23131/24780 | ITL 7.12/7.75/8.48 | out 917.7 | total 25390

(9) DSPARK ACCEPT STATS -- NOT SURFACED through the PD router (limitation, same as prior vLLM PD run). The bench_serving output has NO 'Speculative Decoding' / accept-length section when run against the router (the router forwards only the OpenAI response; server-side spec-decode stats stay inside the decode engine and are not surfaced per-request as they were in the TP8 direct-to-engine run). DSpark is CONFIRMED ACTIVE from the decode engine startup log ('Draft checkpoint bundles a DSpark head; loading draft arch DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark' on all 4 decode ranks) and from the very low/flat ITL (~7.1 ms median at ALL levels) and TPOT (~1.3 ms) that are consistent with the strongly-accepting TP8 run (accept len 5.5-5.8). Documented as a limitation; not a failure.

(10) OBSERVED vs TP8 (both same kou-jing; TP8 from FEAT-002): TPOT median is FLAT and very low on both (TP8 1.20-15.02 rising with conc; PD 1.22-1.33 essentially CONSTANT across all conc) -- PD's dedicated 4 decode cards keep per-token decode latency flat and the ITL p99 tail dramatically calmer (PD ITL p99 7.2-11.0 ms vs TP8 2.36-507.52 ms; the TP8 c16 ITL p99 507 ms tail is GONE under PD, p99 8.48 ms). Trade-off: PD TTFT is much higher and grows with concurrency (prefill is only 4 cards + PD handoff: c16 TTFT med 21.9 s vs TP8 4.2 s) and peak output throughput is lower (PD c16 917.7 vs TP8 763.3 -- actually PD higher here, but PD c8 880 vs TP8 780; mixed). Full cross-topology comparison + verdict is FEAT-004's job; recording raw numbers only here.

(11) END STATE: sglang-pd-prefill (Up, GPU0-3), sglang-pd-decode (Up, GPU4-7, DSpark), sglang-pd-router (Up, :30080 /health=200) ALL LEFT RUNNING. Booking 5bd1f130 left running per boundaries (NO stop/terminate). TP8 artifacts in /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out/ untouched. Instance-side helper scripts written: /opt/dlami/nvme/{launch_pd_prefill.sh,launch_pd_decode.sh,launch_pd_router.sh,sweep_pd.sh,validate_pd_c1.sh}.

BLOCKERS: NONE. PD came up first try with nixl + DSpark-on-decode; none of the troubleshoot fallbacks (switch transfer backend, disable DSpark, adjust mem-fraction) were needed. One minor operational hiccup (not a model blocker): the first background nohup of the c=1 validation died instantly because its stdout was redirected to /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd/validate_c1.runlog before that dir existed (redirect target's parent must pre-exist); FIX: `mkdir -p /opt/dlami/nvme/bench-out-pd` before launching any nohup that logs into it. Applied to the sweep launch too.
